title: Warning Signs That Can't Wait
hook: Serious complications can happen during pregnancy and for up to a year after birth. Knowing the urgent warning signs — and insisting on being heard — can save a life.
key_points: Pregnancy-related complications can occur during pregnancy and up to a year after delivery — not just in the first weeks.
Get care right away for heavy bleeding, chest pain or trouble breathing, a severe or worsening headache, or vision changes.
Also urgent: a fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, severe belly pain, or extreme swelling, dizziness, or leg pain/redness.
Thoughts of harming yourself or the baby are an emergency — speak up, trust your gut, and insist on being heard.
content_html: Most recoveries go smoothly, but serious complications can happen during pregnancy and for up to a year after birth — so the warning signs are worth knowing now. The CDC's Hear Her campaign exists because many of these problems are preventable when concerns are caught and taken seriously.
extra_html: Get medical care right away for heavy vaginal bleeding, chest pain or trouble breathing, a severe headache that won't go away or vision changes, a fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, severe belly pain, extreme swelling of the hands or face, dizziness or fainting, or pain, redness, or swelling in a leg. Thoughts of harming yourself or your baby are an emergency. If you feel like something just isn't right, say so — and if you don't feel heard, say it again or seek a second opinion. Tell any provider you see that you were pregnant within the last year. This is general guidance — when in doubt, contact your doctor or midwife or emergency services; if you have thoughts of harming yourself or the baby, seek help immediately or call 988.

related.title: Healing After Birth Takes Weeks, Not Days
related.hook: Your body just did something huge, and recovery is a season, not a single appointment. Bleeding, cramps, healing, and mood shifts are all part of the fourth trimester.

related.title: Pregnancy Symptoms to Never Ignore
related.hook: A few symptoms in pregnancy mean call your midwife or maternity unit straight away — they can signal serious problems like pre-eclampsia that need checking without delay.

flashcards.prompt: How long after birth can pregnancy-related complications occur?

choices.text: Up to a year after delivery

flashcards.explanation_html: The CDC's Hear Her campaign emphasizes that some problems related to pregnancy can happen up to a year after delivery, so warning signs matter well past birth.

flashcards.prompt: Name some urgent postpartum warning signs that mean 'get care now.'
flashcards.back_html: Heavy bleeding; chest pain or trouble breathing; a severe or worsening headache or vision changes; a fever of 100.4°F or higher; severe belly pain; extreme swelling, dizziness, or leg pain/redness; and thoughts of self-harm.

flashcards.prompt: What should you do if you feel something is seriously wrong but worry about overreacting?

choices.text: Speak up, trust your instincts, and insist on being heard
Wait it out so you don't bother anyone
Only mention it at your next routine visit

flashcards.explanation_html: Many serious complications are preventable when concerns are taken seriously. Trust your gut, say something, and ask to be heard.
